Class SliceProjection

java.lang.Object
edu.cnu.mdi.view.demo.geoslice.SliceProjection
public final class SliceProjection extends Object
Coordinate conversion utilities for the geometry slice demos.

The demos use a simple constant-phi slice through 3D Cartesian geometry. The 2D display convention is: 

    slice x = z
    slice y = radial distance in the selected phi plane

These methods convert between cylindrical/spherical/Cartesian coordinates and the 2D slice coordinates used by the MDI view. They are public so both the 2D MDI view and the companion MDI-3D explanatory view can use the same model and coordinate conventions.

      public static Point cylindrical(double r, double phiDeg, double z)
      Convert cylindrical coordinates to a 3D Cartesian point. 
          x = r cos(phi)
    y = r sin(phi)
    z = z

    • sliceToCartesian

      public static Point sliceToCartesian(Point2D.Double slicePoint, double phiDeg)
      Convert a 2D slice-coordinate point back into a 3D Cartesian point lying in the current constant-phi plane.

      If the slice point is (z, s), where s is the radial coordinate in the current phi plane, then: 

          x = s cos(phi)
    y = s sin(phi)
    z = z
      Parameters:
      slicePoint - point in 2D slice world coordinates
      phiDeg - current slice azimuth, in degrees
      Returns:
      corresponding 3D Cartesian point

      public static double thetaDeg(Point p)
      Compute the spherical polar angle theta in degrees.

      The convention is the usual physics/detector convention: theta = 0 points along positive z, and theta = 90 lies in the x-y plane.

      Returns:
      theta in degrees
